posts.author: European Commission
posts.text:
Justice must be fair, accessible and effective. 

This European Day of Justice, we highlight how justice protects our rights and upholds the rule of law in Europe and beyond. 

From supporting fair trials to strengthening cross-border judicial cooperation, the EU works to ensure access to justice. 

The International Criminal Court, announced as the laureate of the Sakharov Prize, also highlights the importance of accountability and human rights worldwide. 

More: https://link.europa.eu/QBPkPK

media.alt:
Paris, le 22 octobre 2026

Le Premier ministre
à
destinataires in fine

Madame, Monsieur,

Les émeutes urbaines survenues dans plusieurs villes de France lors de la journée de mobilisation du 17 octobre 2026 qui se sont poursuivies le dimanche 18 octobre ont mis en évidence la conjonction de plusieurs mouvements revendicatifs et contestataires, attisés par des éléments violents et particulièrement déterminés. D'autres individus ont profité des désordres générés pour casser, dégrader, incendier, saccager et piller.

A l'évidence, plusieurs réseaux sociaux ont joué un rôle décisif non seulement dans la cristallisation et la viralité de mots d'ordre illicites mais aussi comme leviers de coordination opérationnelle des violences au cours des manifestations (organisation des pillages, échanges sur les cibles, déplacement des groupes ou positions des forces de l'ordre).

Dans l'hypothèse où de tel évènements devaient se reproduire, je souhaite pouvoir disposer de la faculté de suspendre temporairement l'accès à ces services en cas de réitération de violences urbaines. Il s'agirait de bloquer temporairement l'accès aux applications Snapchat, TikTok et Instagram par un filtrage de leurs noms de domaine (DNS), en ménageant dans la mesure du possible les accès Internet fixes à ces applications et, en tout état de cause, l'accès aux autres sites et services Internet sur les réseaux fixes comme mobiles.

Afin de préparer une telle mesure, qui pourrait être décidée le week-end des 24 et 25 octobre en fonction du contexte opérationnel, je vous demande d'anticiper dès aujourd'hui les opérations techniques nécessaires pour la mettre en œuvre. Il s'agit de vous mettre en mesure, si j'en donne l'instruction, de procéder sans délai à la suspension temporaire des services concernés, pour une durée de quelques heures.

Je souhaite que vous me fassiez connaître les conditions techniques dans lesquelles vous pourriez mettre en œuvre une telle suspension. Il convient en effet de procéder à une suspension la plus ciblée possible, sans introduire de distorsion entre opérateurs.

Chaque opérateur devra également être en mesure d'interrompre immédiatement la mesure si celle-ci menace gravement le fonctionnement de son réseau.

Les conditions juridiques dans lesquelles pourrait intervenir cette décision pourront être précisés à vos directeurs juridiques dans une réunion dédiée organisée le 23 octobre.

Je vous serais reconnaissant de bien vouloir garder la confidentialité nécessaire à la préparation de cette mesure, qui ne revêt, à ce stade, qu'un caractère exploratoire.

Je vous prie d'accepter, Madame, Monsieur, l'expression de mes sentiments les meilleurs.

Sébastien LECORNU


Destinataires

Madame Christel HEYDEMANN, directrice générale du groupe ORANGE

Monsieur Benoît TORLOTING, directeur général du groupe BOUYGUES TELECOM

Monsieur Thomas REYNAUD, directeur général du groupe Iliad (FREE)

Monsieur Arthur DREYFUSS, président-directeur général d'Altice France (SFR)

"When I started doing open-source, it was fun. And it kind of still is. But the environment has shifted. Open-source sometimes feels like exploitation. What I would like to see is to find a new model where people working on open-source would be awarded for their work and the hours and hours they put into it from the people who most benefit from their work. I would like companies to realize that this is exploitation. Any exploitation is not sustainable. And it will end up badly if this continues, because the people doing the open-source will stop being motivated to actually do anything in the end."

Open-Source-Software muss finanziert werden wie Infrastruktur, nicht wie ein Hobby.

Wer Milliarden verdient, weil er unter anderem auf Open Source setzt, sollte nicht nur bei der Reparatur helfen, sondern auch bezahlen.

Und für das Wissen über Sicherheitslücken, die am Ende uns alle betreffen, braucht es klare, öffentliche Regeln.￼

1️⃣ PHP ist Open Source: kostenlos und frei für alle. Konzerne, die es einsetzen, verdienen Milliarden. Behörden und Krankenhäuser setzen darauf.

Die PHP-Stiftung hatte zuletzt Ausgaben von rund 870.000 US-Dollar bei Einnahmen von nur gut 730.000 Dollar - von 536 Sponsoren und Einzelspendern, deren Zahl rückläufig war. Das sind also die finanziellen Bedingungen, unter denen eine Software gepflegt wird, ohne die ein großer Teil des Netzes nicht laufen würde.￼

embedded.author: Stefan Münz
embedded.text:
In #Tschechien sind rechtsextreme Parteien bereits mit an der Macht, und ähnlich wie die AfD gehört es zu deren Plan, den gebührenfinanzierten öffentlich-rechtlichen Rundfunk abzuschaffen. Zwar versichern die regierenden Parteien, nur die Finanzierung ändern zu wollen, ohne in die redaktionellen Inhalte einzugreifen. Doch andere Beispiele, etwa Ungarn unter Orban, haben in den vergangenen Jahren gezeigt, wohin so was führt. Deshalb kämpfen nun tschechische BürgerInnen für den Erhalt des gebührenfinanzierten Rundfunks. 
#Medien #ÖRR #Tschechien

I’ve updated my FreeBSD ZFS Bootstrap scripts. There’s now an iso and a memstick version. Nothing fundamental has changed. Cleanup, few disk / zfs settings were made explicit rather than relying on defaults. 

You should still read through and adapt as needed.

The reason I use the script rather than the installer is that I want just one ZFS volume for the OS and not separate volumes for /var /usr etc. Jails will get a dedicated volume each.

https://codeberg.org/hukl/freebsd-toolbox/src/branch/main/freebsd_zfs_bootstrap_iso.sh

https://codeberg.org/hukl/freebsd-toolbox/src/branch/main/freebsd_zfs_bootstrap_memstick.sh

Set `session.upload_progress.enabled=0` until the next PHP release to block an unlikely RCE vector (CVE-2026-115560).

We already recommended this for CVE-2026-109619 from Wednesday: keep it disabled.

Only applications with non-default `serialize_handler` switching it to `php` at runtime can be affected.

There is more information in the advisory on the PHP website by the PHP security team: https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-23-1

embedded.author: Peter Spork
embedded.text:
Seit dem Jahr 2018 gab es in Marokko eine ganzjährige Sommerzeit. Darunter scheint die Bevölkerung zunehmend gelitten zu haben. Vor allem klagte sie darüber, morgens immer wieder schon im Dunkeln aufstehen zu müssen. Die Erfahrungen erinnern an das, was die Menschen in Russland zwischen 2011 und 2014 erlebten, als auch dort die ganzjährige Sommerzeit galt. Nachdem sich in Marokko mehr als 300.000 Menschen an einer Petition zur Rückkehr in die dauerhafte Normalzeit beteiligt hatten, handelte die Regierung. Sie beschloss, am 20. September 2026 in die Normalzeit zurückzukehren. Auch eine zeitweilige Rückkehr zur sogenannten Sommerzeit ist nicht geplant.

Damit wurde in Marokko umgesetzt, was die internationale Allianz für natürliche Zeit – ein Zusammenschluss von Organisationen aus aller Welt – gemeinsam mit Forschenden aus den Bereichen #Chronobiologie und #Schlafforschung  seit langem fordern.

Die wichtigsten Antworten zum Thema Uhrenumstellung (#Zeitumstellung) findet ihr hier: https://www.riffreporter.de/de/wissen/sommerzeit

Les Ecologistes, La France insoumise, le Parti socialiste, le parti communiste, Debout (le parti de François Ruffin), L’Après (parti des ex-insoumis) et Génération.s ont déposé conjointement un recours en référé-liberté contre ces consignes.
embedded.html:
Manifestations du 24 octobre : sept partis politiques de gauche déposent un recours auprès du Conseil d’Etat contre les interdictions de manifester

Les Ecologistes, La France insoumise, le Parti socialiste, le parti communiste, Debout (le parti de François Ruffin), L’Après (parti des ex-insoumis) et Génération.s ont déposé conjointement un recours en référé-liberté contre ces consignes.

media.alt:
Interdictions de manifester : sept partis politiques de gauche déposent un recours auprès du Conseil d’Etat

Le président de la République a affirmé, jeudi, à l’issue d’un conseil de sécurité que « la recommandation générale, c’est qu’il n’y ait pas de manifestation dans les jours à venir ». Il a ajouté que les demandes de manifestations formulées par « des gens qui n’ont aucune légitimité pour cela » seront refusées et que celles venant d’organisations syndicales se verront proposer des circuits alternatifs. « Quand ce ne sont pas des organisations syndicales, partout où on le peut, on interdira », a-t-il insisté.

Les Ecologistes, La France insoumise, le Parti socialiste, le parti communiste, Debout (le parti de François Ruffin), L’Après (parti des ex-insoumis) et Génération.s ont déposé conjointement un recours en référé-liberté contre ces consignes, a expliqué à l’Agence France-Presse la députée Ecologiste Léa Balage El Mariky, qui juge « très inquiétant de restreindre le droit de manifestation, en fonction de qui la déclare ».

Les partis attaquent sur deux points : « l’incompétence » du président de la République à donner des instructions aux préfets, car « ce n’est pas sa fonction constitutionnelle » ; et « l’illégalité » de cette interdiction « en fonction de la typologie des déclarants des manifestations ».

« La liberté de manifester n’est pas une faveur accordée par le pouvoir, c’est un droit constitutionnel. Le Conseil d’Etat l’a déjà rappelé : une interdiction doit être exceptionnelle, proportionnée, et justifiée par des risques avérés, pas par l’identité de l’organisateur », insistent les Ecologistes dans un communiqué. « Comme d’autres associations qui ont saisi le Conseil d’Etat hier, nous demandons au juge administratif de suspendre immédiatement cette consigne », ajoutent les Ecologistes.

Mme Balage El Mariky précise que Place publique, le parti de Raphaël Glucksmann, a été sollicité, mais n’a pas souhaité se joindre à la requête.

(Le Monde)

Handy klingelt. Nummer meiner Bank. Hm. Ich gehe dran und melde mich. Antwort: "Schönen Guten Tag Herr U. Ich rufe an wegen einer Sicherheitslücke und brauche ihre Mithilfe." Ich: "Schönen Guten Tag, ist das Wetter bei Ihnen auch stürmisch?" "Als eine KI habe ich keinen realen Aufenthaltsort und kann Ihnen daher keine Auskunft geben." "Doch, das war genau die richtige Auskunft. Auf Wiedersehen." 🤣

Funfact. Bis zu dieser Antwort war ich sogar einigermaßen sicher, einen Menschen am anderen Ende zu haben. Akustisch wird es schwieriger, KI zu erkennen. Aber es bleiben Maschinen. Direkt meine Bank informiert.

Bei überraschenden Anrufen frage ich immer nebenbei nach Wetter oder anderen obskuren Dingen. Meist um die Leute zu verwirren. #scam

embedded.author: Elena Rossini on GoToSocial ⁂
embedded.text:
Total honest question to my dear Fedi friends, I need a genuine answer, please do not sugarcoat things. I need Dutch bluntness here!

So you have been following #MySoCalledSudoLife adventures for almost two years now.

I'm not sure how to define myself anymore because I'm not an expert at this stuff, but I am no longer a newbie either. Yesterday I updated all my systems using CLI (in tmux)!

Now, my main point after my long preamble:

I want to create custom apparel for the next #FOSDEM, as an act of rebellion against the rejection for our proposal of a DEIB room.

I used to make sweatshirts and t-shirts to promote the visibility of women in film, like: "this is what a film director looks like" or just t-shirts that read "film director". I gifted them to prominent women in film, who LOVED them and wore them on set!

I'd like to do something similar but for FOSDEM / tech.

Is it too much to say: "this is what a sysadmin looks like"? Can I call myself a sysadmin, or would you find it sacrilegious?

Anything else? Like, other suggestions along the lines of "this is what a ----- looks like" or "sysadmin"?

Thanks! 🙏​

media.alt:
"Soon, he began to notice Gloria’s memory deteriorating. She missed social appointments she’d confirmed hours earlier, forgot the PIN number she had used her entire adult life, reached for words that wouldn’t form. The change was so swift he feared that she’d had a stroke without realizing it or that dementia had crept in. He took her to her primary-care doctor, and she was given a mini cognitive test, which she passed. The doctor assured him nothing serious was happening, so Jim began investigating on his own — which is when he realized his mother’s Facebook timeline was littered with 2 a.m. time stamps. He concedes it’s difficult, if not impossible, to draw the line between behavior directly caused by social-media use and the natural effects of aging. Still, he is convinced her screen-time binges were disrupting her sleep and if not directly causing her memory loss, at least worsening it. “It was taking away from her,” he says. That was when he intervened.
Gloria’s generation is the first to enter its most vulnerable years with unfettered access to the internet and, like the rest of us, it has trouble looking away. Americans over 60 now spend more than half their leisure hours in front of screens. But unlike millennials and most Gen-Xers, who have spent years navigating engagement bait, stealth marketing, and AI slop — and have developed a working instinct for what to trust — older adults tend to have little idea of what they’re looking at."
From : NY mag / Intelligencer

embedded.author: T-RREx - Trans Radical Resource Exchange
embedded.text:
JUSTICE FOR
THE
DOLLS

We stand in solidarity with The Dolls of Berlin and queer community centre Casa Kuà.

(⬇️ donation links at the bottom of the post)

The Dolls is a transfem community in Berlin that also does education on (DIY) HRT, these are essential resources for trans people in need of healthcare.

Last Sunday, Casa Kuà, the place where The Dolls held their event, got raided by the police. Everyone present got ID'ed, and detained. Allegedly, HRT and supplies were confiscated. Trans healthcare is not a crime, it's a bogus charge. The Dolls were doing nothing illegal, yet they were met with state violence.

The events of Stonewall and the Institut für Sexualwissenschaft are repeated right before our eyes.

Healthcare is a right, but all too often people do not have access to it. For trans healthcare this is unfortunately commonplace. Some are required to find healthcare outside of systems that are inaccessible and gatekeeping.

This will happen, period. You cannot stop people from seeking and getting life-saving gender-affirming healthcare. But there is a difference in whether this happens with the guidance of a loving and caring community or not.

HRT education, injection safety and trans communtiy are crucial and life saving. The Dolls are here to stay!

The Dolls and Casa Kuà have a fundraiser. And they could really use the money, also for potential legal expenses. So if you can spare an euro or two, or more, that'd be really nice and cool.

https://www.gofundme.com/f/the-dolls-berlin
https://www.gofundme.com/f/casa-kua

We stand with The Dolls. Community is not illegal. Healthcare is not a crime.
International solidarity!

Der Thermostat misst die Zimmertemperatur und regelt die Heizung so, dass die gewünschte Temperatur erreicht wird. Wird es immer Zimmer zu warm, dreht der Thermostat die Heizung automatisch wieder zu.

#MrWissen2go #funk #ZDF #Heizung

media.alt: Grafik mit dem Titel „Das bedeuten die Zahlen auf eurer Heizung“. Zu sehen sind cremeweiße Heizkörperthermostate auf blaugrauem Hintergrund, die von links nach rechts eine höhere Stufe und Temperatur zeigen. Erster Regler mit Schneeflocken-Symbol und der Ziffer 1: „Frostschutz“, „≈ 6 °C“. Zweiter Regler mit Schneeflocke, Ziffer 1, Mond-Symbol und Ziffer 2: „≈ 12 °C“. Dritter Regler mit den Ziffern 1, 2 und 3 und dem Mond-Symbol zwischen 1 und 2: „gilt als optimale Temperatur für nachts“, „≈ 14 °C“. Am rechten Rand ist ein vierter Regler angeschnitten, seine Beschriftung beginnt mit „≈ 16“. Die Grafik geht auf der nächsten Folie weiter.

Fortsetzung der Grafik zu den Zahlen auf der Heizung: weitere cremeweiße Thermostatregler auf blaugrauem Hintergrund. Am linken Rand ist ein Regler angeschnitten, der ≈ 16 °C anzeigt. Der nächste Regler zeigt die Ziffern 2, 3 und 4 mit einem Sonnen-Symbol über der 3: „gilt als optimale Tagestemperatur“, „≈ 20 °C“. Danach folgt ein Regler mit den Ziffern 3, 4 und 5: „ca. + 1 °C pro Strich“, „≈ 24 °C“. Die Anmerkung weist auf einen der kleinen Striche zwischen den Ziffern. Der letzte Regler zeigt die Ziffern 4 und 5: „≈ 28 °C“.

It's time for C to go.

embedded.author: David Hembrow
embedded.text:
So today some of the worst people on earth using the most environmentally destructive tools on earth brought down a huge part of the internet by exploiting a potential problem found many years ago in PHP which was previously not practical for anyone to exploit.

It only became "practical" to exploit this problem because "AI" came along to automate the boring and repetitive work required to do so. Absurd amounts of computing power were applied specifically to break into other peoples' websites.

Now the same people who are behind this are trying to pretend that they're heroes for finding an exploit.

"AI uncovers critical vulnerabilities", their headline reads. But the vulnerability was only made to be critical by the very same people as hide behind that headline.

Many thousands of websites are offline, many people are losing money, many thousands of people are working hard to try to patch or work around the problem, many small guys are finding it almost impossible to patch, and we're all supposed to be thankful to OpenAI and others involved ? Nah. Fuck off.

Everything about "AI" involves a lot of externalized costs, but I've still yet to see even a single positive thing that has been achieved by "AI". That has definitely not changed today.
#php2shell #php #fuckai #openai

The PHP #security issue shows once again how much our society relies on mostly volunteer work. 

Look at PHP Foundation @thephpf finances: 
https://opencollective.com/phpfoundation#category-BUDGET  

- Reimbursed $67K on development work this year
- Received: $642,755 last year

Compare these numbers with the amounts companies have made with products & services built upon #PHP.  Our digital foundations are built on the backs of #opensource volunteers. Governments & companies need to invest in our common digital infrastructures.

Another ran searches while he was suspended (and later fired) after killing a 15-year-old boy.

posts.text:
Under EU digital law, Booking.com must properly assess and address risks linked to fraudulent listings and phishing scams.

It must also clearly label listings that have paid for a higher position in search results.

Booking a holiday should be exciting, not risky. Europeans deserve to book with confidence, knowing platforms are taking their safety seriously. We’ll make sure they live up to their responsibilities.

🔗 More: https://link.europa.eu/md8rtp

My child is at that age (5 almost 6) when girls start experiencing a confidence gap. I would have been a proud mamma to show her the incredible diversity of presenters in our devroom at FOSDEM. 

I’ve been showing her examples of other kinds of excellence (than stereotypical cis white men - sorry no offense) since she was an infant. 

But it’s so much more powerful when you discuss people you know IRL and can show actual examples...

posts.author: Elena Rossini 🌈
posts.text:
2/4

I LOVED tinkering with computers in my childhood and teenage years and it never even occurred to me I could have gotten into computer science or engineering. I didn’t have any examples of that. I chose Mass Communication instead.

It’s only now, many many years later, that I have discovered the world of FOSS (thanks to the Fediverse) and self-hosting. I’m having so much fun and I almost wish I could turn back the clock and study to become a sysadmin (my heroes!)

posts.text:
Not to sound overdramatic but with each passing hour I’m getting more and more saddened by the rejection of the DEIB devroom that we proposed at #FOSDEM (an initiative driven by @RosannaSibora and @Gina)

It would have been so powerful to have a DEIB (Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging) track - to promote the visibility of a different kind of folks in tech AND celebrate them at Europe’s largest open source gathering.

A mini 🧵🥲

🚨 Please read & act if you're running a small online shop in the EU or are even just a customer of one: These people need your urgent support. Otherwise the still new EU-wide packaging & waste regulation (PPWR) as it currently stands and is in full effect WILL kill most of the small businesses in the EU, incl. the livelihoods of artists, designers, illustrators, makers etc. who're trying to survive by selling physical goods online...

The legislation already came online in August, but it's been an utter bureaucratic mess! Official communication and clarification was even worse/absent for many weeks since rollout. An exemption from the most damaging parts for nano/micro-businesses was only voted[1][2] on in parliament today (almost 60(!) days after introduction), but with positive outcome. However, this support by parliament is only a small win and we need more pressure on MEPs to clarify the severity of this situation for the next round(s) of negotiation with the EU Council and member states.

To clarify: The most damaging & costly part of this regulation is the requirement for a legal representative in each EU country you want to ship to. The cost of a single representative is several hundred Euro per yer per country. If you're intending to sell to the entire EU, that's worst case 27 middlemen to pay, i.e. (tens of) thousands of Euro in just regulatory fees every single year. It's completely unrealistic, disproportional, nonsensical and against every aspect of the single market principles... It is now easier to sell to outside the EU than it is to sell inside the EU! Make it make sense!

The only people this regulation benefits are major retailers and the growing compliance industry!

Please boost for visibility! Thank you! 🙏

(Update: added link, punctuation)

[1] https://packaging-journal.de/en/the-european-parliament-wants-to-simplify-the-epr-requirements-only-for-small-companies/
[2] https://www.rapporteur.com/news/meps-back-small-business-exemption-from-costly-waste-reduction-compliance/

#PPWR #EU #SME #SaveMicroEnterprises #Legislation #WriteToYourMEP

media.alt:
Une réponse législative après un week-end de violences ? Le projet de loi dit « casseurs-payeurs » démarre ce mercredi son parcours parlementaire en commission au Sénat, où il pourrait déjà être durci. Mardi, le premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, jugeait devant les députés son texte « absolument indispensable », se disant déterminé à le mener « à son terme » au cours des prochains mois.
Le gouvernement veut créer une responsabilité collective pour toute personne appartenant à un groupement ayant commis des dégradations, sans qu’il y ait besoin de prouver qu’elle en ait commis elle-même. Cette nouvelle forme de responsabilité civile, assortie de plusieurs conditions, serait plafonnée à 10 000 euros par personne, redevables à la victime, aux assureurs, voire à l’Etat s’il se retourne contre l’auteur.

La commission des lois du Sénat, dominé par une alliance entre la droite et les centristes, devrait l’adopter largement, à huis clos, en fin de matinée, en y apportant diverses modifications. Mais les débats les plus importants auront lieu dans l’Hémicycle, mardi 27 octobre, avec de profondes divergences en vue.
Le projet gouvernemental entend aussi mobiliser les allocations familiales et les aides personnelles au logement des fauteurs de troubles qui ne pourraient pas payer. Une circulaire a déjà été annoncée lundi par le gouvernement pour déduire des aides sociales versées les revenus tirés du recel des pilleurs.

posts.author: hukl
posts.text:
In other news: I’ve added a little lua function to my rspamd which checks sender names of received emails against a list of trusted contacts (email - name). If a mail arrives with a sender name which is on the list, the lua function checks if the email address matches. If not it’s marked as spam and a (UN)TRUSTED_SENDER flag is added

Mails from senders that are not on my trusted_senders.map file will use the normal rspam pipeline

That feels like it should be a default feature, right?

Wenn ich morgens zur Arbeit fahre läuft auf Deutschlandfunk Nova immer die Aktion, in der Hörer*innen 10 Minuten mit ihrem Thema und drei Songs selbst gestalten können. Und zum einen ist da immer tolle Aufwachmusik dabei: Curtis Mayfield - Move On Up oder Queen - Don't stop me now. 
Aber auch Geschichten der Menschen sind oft spannend: Der junge Mitarbeiter einer Sicherheits- und Wachfirma, der von seinen Arbeitsbedingungen erzählt oder die Transfrau aus Ostdeutschland, die von Outing und Transition erzählt. 
Da geht am frühen Morgen irgendwie ne ganze Menge mehr als das übliche Frühstücksradio mit Gute-Laune-Phrasen und Heavy Rotation.

👉 https://www.deutschlandfunknova.de/nova-auf-die-eins

#DeutschlandfunkNova #Radio #Hörtipp

embedded.author: Rosanna Sibora
embedded.text:
As I reflected on what I experienced at #FOSDEM, the idea of organizing a devroom dedicated to #diversity was born.

Together with @Gina @_elena  we submitted the proposal to organise a #DEI devroom at #FOSDEM27. It got rejected. 😢💔

Every year we leave #FOSDEM inspired by the people we meet & the passion for #opensource. And every year we also find ourselves thinking about how much greater it could be if more people with different perspectives were part of those conversations.

Es gibt da eine Druckerei, von der sich mindestens 900 Rechnungen über Flyer, Faltblätter, Rollups etc. im Leak befinden - sprich, die für die AfD das Promomaterial druckt.

"Wir machen Druck"

Konnte man schon vorher wissen, hatte ich aber nicht mitbekommen:

Senayt Kesete, SPD-Kandidatin in Frankfurt, hatte im Februar bei WMD ein Plakat für ihren Kommunalwahlkampf in Auftrag gegeben, dass ihr aber nie geliefert wurde.

Bis sie per Telefon die Auskunft bekam: "Die AfD ist unser größter Auftraggeber - das ist doch bekannt."

(LinkedIn-Post: https://de.linkedin.com/posts/senayt-kesete-388811225_spd-graesnen-demokratie-activity-7422657508709900288-kpkz/)

WMD partnert/sponsort den VfB Stuttgart & andere Sportvereine. Der Fußballverein SG Sonnenhof Großaspach hat sein Stadion in WIRmachenDRUCK Arena umbenannt. Kriegt auch immer wieder allerlei Preise - https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/WIRmachenDRUCK

Und da kommt das Geld ins Spiel. Während Tesla und China gar nicht erst versuchen uns bei der Altechnologie Konkurrenz zu machen, investieren sie Forschung und Entwicklung voll in Zukunftstechnologien. Jeder investierte Euro geht in Zukunft.
In Europa hingegen geht nur ein Teil der F&E-Mittel* in Zukunftstechnologie.

posts.text: La police a tenté d'arrêter Raphaël Arnault :
posts.html: La police a tenté d'arrêter Raphaël Arnault :

media.alt:
Communiqué du groupe parlementaire de La France insoumise publié le 20 octobre 2026 : 

« Tentative de mise en scène d'une arrestation du député Raphaël Arnault : la bascule autoritaire du pouvoir

Nous avons appris ce matin que le député du Vaucluse Raphaël Arnault, en route depuis sa circonscription vers l'Assemblée nationale pour participer aux travaux de la session parlementaire, aurait été la cible d'une tentative d'interpellation policière planifiée sur les quais de la gare de Lyon, a la descente de son train. Celle ci n'aurait échoué qu'en raison d'une erreur de la police quant a la rame dans laquelle voyageait le député insoumis, totalement ignorant de ce projet.

Il s'agit manifestement d'un nouveau projet de mise en scène grossière d'arrestation par surprise d'un parlementaire insoumis par le pouvoir. Nous rappelons que la députée européenne Rima Hassan fut visée par une même tentative il y a quelques semaines dans un aéroport. Nous nous interrogeons sur le respect des règles de l'immunité parlementaire dans ces circonstances.

Raphaël Arnault n'a rien à cacher et se tient comme toujours à la disposition de la justice.

Nous questionnons avec gravité le moment de cette tentative. Elle évoque un coup monté après plusieurs déclarations du Premier ministre visant nommément le député Raphaël Arnault. Cela au lendemain des révélations de Mediapart documentant une tentative d'instrumentalisation gouvernementale des services de renseignements pour atteindre La France insoumise et de l'appel du Président du Sénat à interdire la principale force d'opposition de gauche de notre pays. Incapable de répondre aux revendications populaires légitimes et d'assurer la paix publique dans le pays, la macronie a manifestement fait le choix de criminaliser l'opposition pour assurer sa survie politique. Nous alertons tous les démocrates sur la gravité de cette bascule autoritaire des mœurs du gouvernement. Nous assurons Raphaël Arnault de notre plein soutien. »

media.alt:
"Le maire de Paris Centre, Ariel Weil, souhaite un couvre-feu et suggère l’intervention de l’armée

Le maire de Paris Centre, Ariel Weil (Parti socialiste), dont le secteur a été durement touché par les pillages et les destructions ce week-end, a déclaré avoir demandé dès dimanche l’instauration d’un couvre-feu, et « pourquoi pas » l’intervention de l’armée pour empêcher que de telles scènes se reproduisent.

« Il y a eu une casse incroyable, même à l’apogée des “gilets jaunes”, on n’a pas connu une telle casse en un seul week-end », a décrit sur BFM-TV le maire de Paris Centre, qui regroupe les quatre premiers arrondissements de la capitale. L’édile a précisé avoir demandé « dès hier », dimanche, la mise en place d’un couvre-feu, « et même, pourquoi pas, la sollicitation de l’armée », même si « évidemment ce n’est pas l’idéal ».

« Si, à un moment donné, on est pris de court, qu’on n’a pas assez de moyens, il vaut mieux un couvre-feu, la présence de l’armée, pour suppléer aux forces de l’ordre, qu’une nouvelle nuit de pillages comme celle qu’on a connues ces deux dernières nuits », a ajouté M. Weil."

(Le Monde)

embedded.author: cpu
embedded.text:
@icing a thing I'm still grieving is the world where when someone reported a bug/vuln it was typically because either A) they were a user of the software, and bumped into the issue B) they thought harder about the code than I had when I wrote it, and found something overlooked. Some combination of those factors helped alleviate the feeling of "damn, I fucked up".

I'm all for improving things but the wave of input from drive-by "people" that are both divorced from the purpose/use of the software, and have also spent no time doing any real analysis of their own sucks... It wears you down in a uniquely new way and there's nothing compensating for the negative feelings.

posts.author: Steffen Voß
posts.text: "Wieso bricht meine Reichweite ein," fragen sich die Leute auf kommerziellen Plattformen und sie tauschen Tipps aus, wie man "den Algorithmus" austrickst, um noch Leute zu erreichen. Im #Fediverse gilt ausschließlich: "Um Leute zu erreichen, musst du Leute erreichen." - Natürlich gibt es auch hier bessere und schlechtere Posts. Ein gutes Bild oder eine gute Linkvorschau helfen. Der Text muss schnell zugänglich sein und leider funktionieren auch hier Aufreger besser als #GoodNews... Aber hier muss man nicht bestimmte Wörter oder Themen meiden, um geshadowbannt zu werden. Man kann einfach Links benutzen - nicht "im ersten Kommentar". Man muss nicht regelmäßig, jeden Tag, einmal die Woche oder so posten, damit die Reichweite nicht einschläft... Das hat etwas Befreiendes.

posts.text:
Women shouldn't have to anticipate violence. 

This month marks three years since the EU joined the Istanbul Convention, a landmark treaty recognising gender-based violence against women as a violation of human rights. 

It sets out concrete measures to prevent it, to protect victims, and hold perpetrators accountable.  

Our goal is clear:  a world where women can live free from fear. 🧡 

🔗 Learn more about the Istanbul Convention: https://www.coe.int/en/web/istanbul-convention/key-facts

posts.text:
The NFL is urging the Supreme Court to hear New Jersey’s case over whether states can regulate prediction markets, complaining that Kalshi refused to ban easily manipulated bets and expressing concerns over consumer protection and game integrity.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter
posts.html:
The NFL is urging the Supreme Court to hear New Jersey’s case over whether states can regulate prediction markets, complaining that Kalshi refused to ban easily manipulated bets and expressing concerns over consumer protection and game integrity.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter

media.alt:
In prediction markets
As New Jersey petitions the Supreme Court to take up the issue of whether state gambling laws should apply to prediction markets, it’s found a new ally in the National Football League. The NFL filed an amicus brief urging the Court to take up the case, arguing that sports contracts in prediction markets create new risk, rather than hedge existing risk, and therefore should be regulated by state gambling commissions. They detail complaints around Kalshi’s refusal to comply with their requests to ban bets that are easily manipulated, those involving injuries or referees, and those whose outcomes can be known in advance. They also note that Kalshi’s platform allows participants who are 18 or older, despite many state gambling laws that restrict betting to 21 and older.16

Unlike Major League Baseball and the National Hockey League, which have signed sponsorship or trademark deals with prediction markets, the NFL has been more hesitant. NFL games have drawn huge volumes on prediction markets, with the league’s games accounting for $1.8 billion of the $3.3 billion total prediction market volume on the first Sunday of the most recent NFL season. According to their brief, this is all the more reason for the NFL to worry about the emergence of such platforms, which they say undermine efforts to protect bettors, ensure wagers are fair, and limit threats to the integrity of the games themselves.16

Daniel Wallach, a gaming lawyer who focuses on sports betting, said that the NFL’s encouragement “meaningfully” increases the chances the Supreme Court will hear the case. He added, “It is extremely telling that the sports league which has most forcefully advocated for federal regulation is essentially saying ‘this ain’t it’.”17

A jury convicted the Uranium Finance exploiter who stole $53M+ and spent it on Magic and Pokémon cards, Roman coins, and a scrap of the Wright brothers’ plane that went to the moon. His “code is law” defense wasn’t helped by him admitting to the exploit and calling crypto “all fake internet money anyway.”

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter
posts.html:
A jury convicted the Uranium Finance exploiter who stole $53M+ and spent it on Magic and Pokémon cards, Roman coins, and a scrap of the Wright brothers’ plane that went to the moon. His “code is law” defense wasn’t helped by him admitting to the exploit and calling crypto “all fake internet money anyway.”

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter

media.alt:
Everything else
A jury has convicted Jonathan Spalletta, the man who repeatedly exploited the Uranium Finance defi crypto exchange to steal more than $53 million [I78, W3IGG], which he then used to buy Magic: The Gathering and Pokémon cards, antique Roman coins, and a scrap of fabric from the original Wright brothers’ airplane that was later taken by Neil Armstrong to the surface of the moon. While Spalletta and his lawyers attempted the classic “code is law” defense, it probably did not help his case that the government was able to produce a message from Spalletta in which he wrote, “I did a crypto heist of $1.5MM a couple of weeks ago ... There was a bug in a smart contract, and I exploited it ... Crypto is all fake internet money anyway.”15

Two evidence photos, one of a “Black Lotus” Magic Card in a protective plastic case inside a plastic zipper bag bearing auction information, and the other of a scrap of yellowed fabric inside a protective case also bearing auction information. Behind the case is a portion of a letter from the Armstrong family attesting to its authenticity.
Caption: Spalletta used the proceeds of his crime to purchase a $500,000 “Black Lotus” Magic card and a $137,500 scrap of fabric from the original Wright brothers’ airplane that was later taken by Neil Armstrong to the surface of the moon (via the US Department of Justice)

Hex founder Richard Heart, who the SEC once accused of spending investor money on sports cars, luxury watches, and the world’s largest black diamond, has been arrested in Istanbul after nearly two years on an Interpol Red Notice over Finnish tax fraud charges. He no longer faces SEC enforcement after the agency effectively dropped his case last year.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter
posts.html:
Hex founder Richard Heart, who the SEC once accused of spending investor money on sports cars, luxury watches, and the world’s largest black diamond, has been arrested in Istanbul after nearly two years on an Interpol Red Notice over Finnish tax fraud charges. He no longer faces SEC enforcement after the agency effectively dropped his case last year.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter

media.alt:
Richard Heart
Richard Heart, the founder of the Hex cryptocurrency scheme, managed to spend nearly two years subject to an Interpol Red Notice before authorities finally nabbed him in Türkiye. The US SEC sued Heart in 2023, noting that asking people to “sacrifice” rather than “invest” their crypto assets in exchange for his PulseChain and Hex tokens was not the get-out-of-securities-laws-free card he seemed to think it was. The lawsuit further alleged he had misappropriated at least $12 million to buy sports cars, luxury watches, and the largest black diamond in the world [I35, 45, 73].11

Photograph of a woman in side profile holding The Enigma black diamond in front of her face. It is an asymmetrical faceted diamond about the size of an egg.
Caption: Heart purchased “The Enigma” for £3.16 million (then around $4.28 million) in February 2022 (via Sotheby’s)

Then, in September 2024, he was accused by Finnish authorities of evading several hundred million euros in taxes, and was named as a suspect in a brutal physical assault on a sixteen-year-old perpetrated in February 2021 [I67].12 At Finland’s request, Heart was added to the EU’s Most Wanted list and an Interpol Red Notice was issued [I72].

Turkish police have now arrested Heart and his wife in Istanbul. While a report from Turkish media outlet the Daily Sabah claims that Heart was wanted by Interpol on crypto fraud charges, the red notice only lists a charge of aggravated tax fraud.1314

Photograph: Richard Heart, wearing a top hat and speaking into a microphone
Caption: Richard Heart

Though Heart is certainly facing serious criminal consequences internationally, his US regulatory woes have eased. In February 2025, a federal judge dismissed the SEC’s lawsuit against Heart, finding the agency hadn’t adequately established that Heart had sufficient ties to the US. Heart thanked Trump for the outcome. Neither Trump nor his gutted SEC had anything to do with that ruling, but Heart may have had something to thank them for later on: in April 2025, the agency declined to amend its complaint to address the jurisdictional issues, effectively abandoning the case as it had so many others against crypto firms [I78, 82].

Trump announced yet another $​TRUMP memecoin gala, plus a Super Bowl suite for top holders. The fine print notes the events don’t mean his companies aren’t dumping the token, which is down 95%, at the same time.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter
posts.html:
Trump announced yet another $​TRUMP memecoin gala, plus a Super Bowl suite for top holders. The fine print notes the events don’t mean his companies aren’t dumping the token, which is down 95%, at the same time.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter

media.alt:
Trump business interests
Trump has announced yet another $TRUMP memecoin “gala dinner” for November, following the inaugural event in May 2025 [I82, Guests] and a second one in April 2026 [I105]. Each has generated less excitement than the last: the memecoin price continues to erode; the previous pricey events offered little more than bragging rights, mediocre food, and subpar company; and the organizers continue to pare back access to Trump himself after drawing criticism over pay-for-access to the president. While these events are intended to juice the token’s price — which has already plummeted more than 95% from its highs — they have become increasingly ineffective, producing shorter and less dramatic price spikes.

Image: Price chart showing that $TRUMP has dwindled more than 95% from its launch-time highs (via CoinMarketCap)

Kevin Mercuri, former spokesperson for Bill Zanker — who runs the $TRUMP memecoin and related portions of Trump’s personal business empire — criticized the event, calling the gala “tone-deaf” while “the nation is embroiled in a dead-end war and facing a widespread affordability crisis”.7 Trump personally pocketed more than $635 million from the memecoin during the 2025 fiscal year, as nearly all of the roughly one million retail traders lost money — a combined $3.8 billion.8 The fine print in the website now includes a disclaimer that the existence of events like the gala “does not indicate that Fight Fight Fight LLC, CIC Digital LLC or their respective affiliates are not contemporaneously disposing of $TRUMP coins”.9

The Trump memecoin website is also now teasing plans to invite the top 18 holders of the token to watch the Super Bowl from a “private luxury suite” and enjoy a “3-day VIP experience” including dinners and an “elite afterparty”. The fine print is careful to note that “President Donald J. Trump will not be in attendance in the Suite.” The plan is part of the “Trump Coin Club” membership scheme launched in April, which has so far held one event in which holders were invited to a Formula 1 race and “epic music festival” in Singapore [TCC].10

posts.text:
Crypto super PAC Fairshake announced 32 House endorsements: all incumbents, all but four in safe seats. It’s their attempt to pad their win rate and claim it proves the existence of a crypto voter bloc, but they are abandoning reliable allies in tough races.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter
posts.html:
Crypto super PAC Fairshake announced 32 House endorsements: all incumbents, all but four in safe seats. It’s their attempt to pad their win rate and claim it proves the existence of a crypto voter bloc, but they are abandoning reliable allies in tough races.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter

media.alt: Map of the United States showing photos of the 32 House members endorsed by the crypto super PAC Fairshake, each placed on their home state. Red borders mark the 19 Republicans: Ben Cline (Virginia), Troy Downing (Montana), Tom Emmer (Minnesota), Michelle Fischbach (Minnesota), Scott Fitzgerald (Wisconsin), Mike Haridopolos (Florida), Pat Harrigan (North Carolina), French Hill (Arkansas), Bill Huizenga (Michigan), Brian Jack (Georgia), Frank Lucas (Oklahoma), Lisa McClain (Michigan), August Pfluger (Texas), Guy Reschenthaler (Pennsylvania), David Rouzer (North Carolina), Austin Scott (Georgia), Jason Smith (Missouri), Bryan Steil (Wisconsin), and Glenn Thompson (Pennsylvania). Blue borders mark the 13 Democrats: Pete Aguilar (California), Brendan Boyle (Pennsylvania), Janelle Bynum (Oregon), Josh Gottheimer (New Jersey), Steven Horsford (Nevada), Jonathan Jackson (Illinois), Lucy McBath (Georgia), Sarah McBride (Delaware), Jimmy Panetta (California), Hillary Scholten (Michigan), Terri Sewell (Alabama), Suhas Subramanyam (Virginia), and Derek Tran (California).

In elections and political influence
The crypto industry’s flagship super PAC, Fairshake, has announced a list of 32 House candidates it plans to back in the midterms. All of them are incumbents; 13 are Democrats, and 19 are Republicans. All but four are in races dubbed “safe” for them by the Cook Political Report.5

PAC spokesperson Geoff Vetter gave the game away when he bragged to The Hill, “We’ve won 53 of the 57 races we engaged in this cycle”.6 As I’ve noted previously [I68, 70, 108], the crypto PACs and advocacy groups often support shoo-in candidates so that they can later claim that their win rate reflects some silent majority of Americans who support the “crypto agenda”. Similarly, when Coinbase-linked Stand With Crypto endorsed 39 candidates in 2024, The Hill estimated prior to Election Day that 32 of them had a 75% or higher chance of winning [I68].

Out of their list, the Fairshake network has so far spent the most on Republicans Bill Huizenga (MI, $1.5 million) and French Hill (AR, $1.4 million). It has spent around $1 million apiece supporting Bryan Steil (R-WI), Janelle Bynum (D-OR), Derek Tran (D-CA), and Steven Horsford (D-NV), and $512,000 each on Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) and Pete Aguilar (D-CA). Most of the other endorsed candidates have so far received around $75,000 each from the network. Some of the biggest checks went to members who chair the committees with jurisdiction over crypto, including Hill (Financial Services) and Steil (digital assets subcommittee).

Conspicuously missing are several reliable crypto allies in tougher races, including Democrats Don Davis (NC) and Shomari Figures (AL) and Republicans Zach Nunn (IA) and Mike Lawler (NY). Fairshake spent more than $2 million each on Davis and Figures in 2024, and $1 million on Nunn; it didn’t back Lawler. Nunn and Lawler have, however, received smaller amounts of support this cycle from Andreessen Horowitz, one of Fairshake’s biggest backers, through donations by several executives to a crypto-themed joint fundraising committee called “Hodl the Line”.

posts.text:
Community bankers are suing the OCC over its spree of national trust bank charters, at least 13 of 21 of which went to crypto firms (including Trump’s World Liberty). They argue it’s a side door for crypto firms to get the perks of a bank charter without the rules.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter
posts.html:
Community bankers are suing the OCC over its spree of national trust bank charters, at least 13 of 21 of which went to crypto firms (including Trump’s World Liberty). They argue it’s a side door for crypto firms to get the perks of a bank charter without the rules.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter

media.alt:
In regulators
The Independent Community Bankers of America has sued the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency over its recent rulemaking and its spree of national trust bank charters. At least 13 of the 21 charters granted by the OCC under Trump have gone to crypto firms, including Circle, Ripple, and the Trump family’s own World Liberty Financial [I88, 98, 99, 101, 102, 107]. While the national trust bank framework is intended to let firms hold assets on clients’ behalf without the more stringent oversight applied to traditional banks that take deposits and lend them out, the community banks argue that the OCC has overstepped its authority and turned the regime into a backdoor for crypto companies to get the perks of a bank charter without the rules. The suit singles out Protego, which won conditional approval for a trust charter despite plans to offer crypto custody, trading, lending, and asset management services.

The OCC’s expansion “creates a gaping hole in regulation,” the trade group writes, letting crypto firms perform many of the same functions as community banks “while evading the fundamental safeguards, obligations, and oversight of those banks.” Their customers don’t receive the protections of deposit insurance, the separation of banking and commerce, or limits on dealings with risky investments like hedge funds. And because the national charters preempt state law, they lose some state consumer protections. Many won’t realize it: “Customers will reasonably assume that a company having ‘national bank’ in its title is an insured depository institution.”

There’s also very little precedent for what will happen if one of these firms fails. “The OCC has not managed an uninsured bank receivership in nearly one hundred years,” the lawsuit points out, warning that “failures of risky uninsured national trust banks could spread instability throughout the nation’s financial system, including by spreading contagion risks to other traditional banks like community banks.”

The suit also echoes some of the same arguments raised by community banks during the Clarity Act negotiations: that crypto firms, freed from much of the regulatory burden banks carry, will siphon deposits away from community banks and reduce their capacity to lend [I91, 99, 107, 108, 110].

ICBA President and CEO Rebeca Romero Rainey said in a statement that “Congress did not create the national trust charter as a side door into the banking system for crypto firms seeking the credibility of a federal bank charter.” But crypto firms have previously balked at complaints from traditional banks. Last spring, Coinbase’s then-Chief Legal Officer Paul Grewal accused the ICBA of protectionism, writing, “Imagine opposing a regulated trust charter because you prefer crypto to stay … unregulated” [I96, 102].a

A Senate subcommittee is probing Tether’s ties to Cantor Fitzgerald, the firm Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick supposedly divested from by handing it to his sons. Per Senator Blumenthal, Cantor’s 5% stake in Tether has skyrocketed from $600M to ~$10B since Trump returned to office.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter
posts.html:
A Senate subcommittee is probing Tether’s ties to Cantor Fitzgerald, the firm Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick supposedly divested from by handing it to his sons. Per Senator Blumenthal, Cantor’s 5% stake in Tether has skyrocketed from $600M to ~$10B since Trump returned to office.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter

media.alt:
Tether, Howard Lutnick, and Cantor Fitzgerald
Hines isn’t the only Trump official whose ties to Tether are drawing scrutiny. The Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations is probing the relationship between the stablecoin firm and financial giant Cantor Fitzgerald, which was previously headed by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Upon his cabinet appointment, Lutnick claimed to have satisfied his ethics requirements by transferring his interest in the firm to a trust benefiting his four children, and handing control to two of his sons — a move borrowed from Trump. Like Trump, Lutnick has continued to profit from the family business — his 2025 financial disclosure reported a $192 million distribution from the firm. Nor does he seem to have stepped away from it: in April, when the Cantor-funded Fellowship PAC disclosed plans to spend $1.75 million backing Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate primary runoff, senior Republican officials called Lutnick to complain. The PAC quietly dropped the ad three days later [I105].

An October 8 letter from PSI Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal to Cantor Chairman and CEO Brandon Lutnick disclosed that the subcommittee is investigating Cantor Fitzgerald’s relationship with Tether and its connections to the Trump regime.4 Cantor took a 5% stake in the stablecoin issuer in 2024, and according to Blumenthal, “Since the President’s return to office, Cantor Fitzgerald’s five percent stake in Tether has increased in value from $600 million to an estimated $10 billion, in addition to the tens of millions of dollars the company collects every year from the assets it holds for Tether.” The letter raises concerns about Tether’s use by illicit actors, including Iran’s shadow banking system, and about Cantor’s close ties to Lutnick and the rest of the Trump administration.

Blumenthal requested information on Cantor Fitzgerald’s due diligence on Tether’s reserves and anti-money laundering programs, the terms of a loan from Tether to Howard Lutnick that may have financed his transfer of the business to his children [I103], and copies of any communications by Secretary Lutnick involving regulatory matters or with other White House advisors.4

posts.author: Molly White
posts.text:
While Bo Hines shaped the Genius Act as Trump’s crypto council director, his family’s consulting firm took $6.3M+ from Tether. He pushed a change to the law that would primarily benefit Tether, then left to run Tether’s US arm.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter
posts.html:
While Bo Hines shaped the Genius Act as Trump’s crypto council director, his family’s consulting firm took $6.3M+ from Tether. He pushed a change to the law that would primarily benefit Tether, then left to run Tether’s US arm.

#crypo #cryptocurrency #USpol #USpolitics #CitationNeededNewsletter

media.alt:
In the White House
Tether, Bo Hines, and NXUM
Bo Hines, President Trump’s bizarre choice [I72] to serve as the first executive director of his crypto advisory council, was among the key architects of the Genius Act, the stablecoin law signed in July 2025. Hines’ previous qualifications consisted of playing college football, losing two Congressional races, and co-owning a small consulting firm called NXUM with his father. He kept his stake in NXUM when he joined the administration.

The Wall Street Journal has now reported that weeks after Hines began working on the bill, his father and their fellow NXUM co-owner Gary Dennis met with Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino. Tether is the largest stablecoin issuer, and had the most riding on the legislation. Though NXUM previously had little involvement with the crypto sector, it pitched Tether on a “strategic lobbying” and PR campaign that has netted NXUM at least $6.3 million to date, with payments that began while Hines was still at the White House and were split three ways among the co-owners. The final deal omitted any mention of lobbying, and was routed through a separate marketing firm.

Meanwhile, Hines pushed legislators to double the grace period for crypto exchanges to stop offering noncompliant stablecoins — a change that primarily benefited Tether. He also remained active in Signal chats with his NXUM partners. When some Republican congresspeople stalled the bill, his father informed Dennis he’d gotten a “very worried” call from Ardoino and that Tether wanted them to “obliterate” the holdouts. Hours later, Hines sent the NXUM group chat talking points casting the legislators as “undermining the president and ... bought and paid for by democratic shills like coinbase and a16z”. When Trump brokered a deal with the holdouts weeks later, Dennis bragged to an associate, “Bo got it done.” Three weeks after the bill was signed, Hines left the White House; the following month, he was named CEO of Tether’s new US arm.

NXUM has only grown more entangled with Tether since. The consulting firm, which is pitching investors on a deal in which Tether would buy a 25% stake for $56 million, has started branding itself as the “strategic media infrastructure layer behind Tether”. It also helped launch the Fellowship PAC, which is chaired by Jesse Spiro, Tether US’s head of government affairs [Tether PAC]. The PAC is funded almost entirely by Cantor Fitzgerald, an investor in Tether and its primary US financial partner, which was previously run by now-Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. The PAC has paid NXUM more than $6.5 million. Before it launched, Dennis reminded an associate: “Again, no link to Tether, Nxum, Bo”.

Hines was succeeded on the crypto council by Patrick Witt, whose resume likewise featured college football and failed congressional bids [I90]. Witt took over negotiations on the Clarity Act crypto market structure bill, which recently fizzled after falling short of the votes needed for cloture [I110]. In July, the council’s deputy director, Harry Jung, stepped down to join (you guessed it!) NXUM.1 Now, Witt has left his post, presumably to collect his reward. I look forward to learning who’s paying it.

His departure adds to growing nerves in the crypto sector that the White House is losing interest. David Sacks stepped down from his combined “AI and crypto czar” role in March, and earlier this month Trump tapped Jay Clayton to become his AI czar.2 No crypto czar has been named, and the digital assets advisory council is now without a director or deputy director. The Clarity Act is dead, with little hope of being revived after the midterms. If I were among the crypto executives whose money has fueled more than $250 million in super PAC election spending since 2024, I might also be a little worried that the administration got what it needed from me and is now moving on to newer, shinier things.3

posts.author: Prof. Stefan Rahmstorf
posts.text:
Here's 3 surprising new preprints on the Atlantic ocean circulation #AMOC. 🌊The first by Winkelbauer et al. analyses 17 different ocean reanalysis products and finds the AMOC has weakened about 15% over the last 3 decades.
https://egusphere.copernicus.org/preprints/2026/egusphere-2026-5435/

The 2nd by Bell et al. from UK Met Office does a similar analysis using atmospheric reanalysis, deriving #AMOC changes from an energy balance and the heat flux though the ocean surface. The find about 14% AMOC weakening over the past 3 decades.
https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-10854125/v1

A study by Ben-Yami et al. looks for tell-tale signs of approaching an #AMOC tipping point in historic runs of climate models vs. observed SST patterns. They find a loss of stability in the real-world AMOC but not in models, so AMOC in models may be too stable.
https://journals.plos.org/climate/article?id=10.1371/journal.pclm.0000781

embedded.author: Maija Koivula ⌘
embedded.text: @evacide  You are wrong. I did the math and literally thousands of trolls harassing young female Finnish politicians on Facebook all disappeared at once, at the same time, coinciding with the Yandex explosion. For most profiles I’ve taken reports of numbers dropping at face value, but because of your post and others miming it, I went and did the math. There’s a more than 90 % drop on hateful reactions and comments on the first three profiles I came across that the algorithm recommended to me. I’ve been following the troll traffic on young female politicians’ FB pages for two years now because I fear fascists are trying to influence the next Finnish parliamentary elections by making young women especially too scared to show up. Stories which gaslight and underplay real experiences on mass harrassment have come out in Finnish as a result of comments such as this so I actually find this comment somewhat harmful and as badly sourced as half on the original story. Thankfully I have eyes and a brain and I can check these stats myself on Facebook, and seems at least one user here agrees with my observations.

embedded.author: Craig Hockenberry
embedded.text:
FB25129828:

The iPhone Duo lacks an Action Button and folks are looking at ways to replace that functionality. If it's an affordance for a Shortcut or Flashlight, you need an alternative.

Back Tap can be used, but it has a flaw: the display needs to be on before taps are recognized. An Action Button always works.

Now imagine a situation where you want to turn on a flashlight while in an inaccessible area: like finding AirPods under a bed. Back Tap's "display on" requirement is a hindrance.

embedded.author: Thomas Beagle
embedded.text:
Many years ago I used to work on a Cobol-based application that ran over an 80x25 green screen terminal. People running 30 or 40 users on a 486 PC running SCO Unix hooked up to a multi-port serial card.

We'd never have tolerated the amount of waiting between actions or screens that is now considered absolutely normal on web-based cloud-hosted applications.

Weird how things change.

posts.text: I wrote about the AI safety vibe shift. It's been a long time in coming: https://www.platformer.news/ai-safety-vibe-shift-coxon-anthropic/
posts.html: I wrote about the AI safety vibe shift. It's been a long time in coming: https://www.platformer.news/ai-safety-vibe-shift-coxon-anthropic/

media.alt:
Now, excited public conversation (and in particular, public conversation on X) is no
substitute for actual regulation. Congress has a long history of introducing tech regulations
that go nowhere — and of launching probes that go nowhere. And if Christiano's best
efforts at getting OpenAl to self-regulate fall short — well, he won't be the first board
member to have that experience.
Still, I can't help but be heartened by the vibe shift in Al safety. Last month, in the wake of
Mark Zuckerberg's glad-handing treatise on "personal superintelligence," | argued that true
superintelligence is a dragon. And while I remain hopeful that it can be tamed, I believe the
researchers who say we are nowhere close to being sure of it — and are quitting, in protest,
jobs that would make them rich. The right people are now listening to them, and here's
hoping they take action.

posts.author: Casey Newton
posts.text: I wrote about why the AI labs make for lousy messengers about AI safety — and about why we should take them seriously anyway https://www.platformer.news/openai-astra-warning-alignment-monitoring-pachocki/
posts.html: I wrote about why the AI labs make for lousy messengers about AI safety — and about why we should take them seriously anyway https://www.platformer.news/openai-astra-warning-alignment-monitoring-pachocki/

media.alt:
There's the sense of blame-shifting from OpenAl in particular, which is now at the center of
two cases of its agents hacking into thirdnot nots and has sometimes talked about these
incidents more like important research milestones than the acts of negligence that they
were. Is this truly the world's problem to solve, or is it primarily OpenAl's?
There's the persistent belief that, whatever safety lapses a case like the Hugging Face
incident might reveal, the attention nonetheless benefits OpenAl and the Al industry at
large. OpenAl in particular has played into this by arguing that you should respond to the
Hugging Face attack by using more OpenAl products — a case that Greg Brockman made
explicitly, in a blog post. When labs dismiss the idea that they are turning these incidents
into marketing campaigns — well, they're not not using them in marketing campaigns.

posts.author: Casey Newton
posts.text: Wrote about Meta's ludicrous effort to position itself as a leader in child safety after today's $17 billion settlement with state AGs https://www.platformer.news/meta-child-safety-settlement-instagram-facebook-youtube-tiktok/
posts.html: Wrote about Meta's ludicrous effort to position itself as a leader in child safety after today's $17 billion settlement with state AGs https://www.platformer.news/meta-child-safety-settlement-instagram-facebook-youtube-tiktok/

media.alt:
This — along with countless other documented harms — is the actual history of Meta's
treatment of its child users: as a precious resource to be mined, monetized, and analyzed
well beyond what the law allows. No wonder, then, that as of last month, nearly six in 10
Americans support banning under-16s from social media entirely. At least 10 countries have
passed or implemented such bans already, and more are likely to follow.
Viewed in that light, Meta's belated announcement of new limits and safety features is
hardly the "groundbreaking" agreement Mahoney describes it as. Rather, it's a bet that
accepting a small amount of pain will let the company avoid a much larger one. Given the
thousands of lawsuits the company still faces around the country, though, Meta still may be
in for a world of hurt.

posts.author: Casey Newton
posts.text: I wrote about building an LLM wiki to stay on top of my beat. A month in, it's changing how I work https://www.platformer.news/karpathy-llm-wiki-journalism-productivity/
posts.html: I wrote about building an LLM wiki to stay on top of my beat. A month in, it's changing how I work https://www.platformer.news/karpathy-llm-wiki-journalism-productivity/

media.alt:
The result is that I now have more than 1,440 wiki pages covering most of what has ever
interested me at Platformer: from the content moderation focus of the first few years to my
growing interest in child safety and Al progress. The wiki creates detailed timelines that link
to original sources, and I can ask it questions using a simple Obsidian plugin named
Claudian.
How does this make me more productive? I've found it highly useful in fast-evolving,
complex cases like the OpenAl / Hugging Face agentic breach, where we learned a little
more about the story every few days for a matter of weeks. Each day as I prepared to
write, or podcast, or go on someone else's podcast, I would pull up the page and refresh my
memory — while also opening up the original sources to make sure nothing I was about to
say was hallucinated. Given the real complexity of that story - how exactly did the agent
escape? From where? To where? — this saved me tons of time.

posts.text: Town was the first company I saw in a while that made me say ohhhh ... everyone is going to copy this. I interviewed 'mayor' Jean-Denis Greze about building a self-organizing company https://www.platformer.news/town-interview-jean-denis-greze-assistants/
posts.html: Town was the first company I saw in a while that made me say ohhhh ... everyone is going to copy this. I interviewed 'mayor' Jean-Denis Greze about building a self-organizing company https://www.platformer.news/town-interview-jean-denis-greze-assistants/

media.alt:
Newton: Every once in a while, when I'm using productivity software, I have one of these
moments where I think: oh, everyone is going to copy this. And I had that when I saw this
wiki that you built for your customers. Tell us a little about it.
Greze: We cannot claim that the wiki is our original idea — Karpathy and others have talked
about how you can use Al to take a set of documents and build a knowledge base out of
them. Our job is to take this incredible technology and make it accessible to everyone. We
had the wiki in the background for a long time as something that powers the experience —
and it turns out people love reading about themselves, so at some point it just became
natural to expose it.
The single-person version of this is interesting. The multi-person version is even more
interesting. You're talking about building this new company — it's not just what it knows
about each person, which is private information for each person. The company has things
about the business as a whole that everyone could use knowing. Can you do that
automatically? Most companies aren't even on Notion — I love Notion, it's a fantastic
product, but in the world of productivity, it's like 1 percent of companies that are on
something like Notion. How could you give that kind of power to 99 percent of companies,
where it can have a really good understanding of what's happening across the business, so
that everyone can be more effective in their role?

@Mastodon 

Here are the "plain English" guidelines: 

— Any servers that want to use the Mastodon name and logo in their branding (not domain!) should seek express written permission from Mastodon, which is granted on a case-by-case basis.
— The word Mastodon should never be used in the main part of a server’s domain (a subdomain is allowed).** We will not retroactively enforce this on **servers created before May 13, 2026.**
— Existing servers using the Mastodon name in their domain must include this disclaimer: “This [server/site] is not affiliated with or endorsed by Mastodon GmbH or Mastodon Inc.”
— Any fair use mentions or derivative usage of the Mastodon name (such as mstdn) should include the disclaimer.

— Existing servers using the Mastodon name in their domain must include this disclaimer: “This [server/site] is not affiliated with or endorsed by Mastodon GmbH or Mastodon Inc.”
— Any fair use mentions or derivative usage of the Mastodon name (such as mstdn) should include the disclaimer.

posts.text: I wrote about Mark Zuckerberg's facile, self-serving AI manifesto and what he misunderstands about the technology https://www.platformer.news/zuckerberg-ai-manifesto-dragons/
posts.html: I wrote about Mark Zuckerberg's facile, self-serving AI manifesto and what he misunderstands about the technology https://www.platformer.news/zuckerberg-ai-manifesto-dragons/

media.alt:
Zuckerberg pays glancing attention to risks, suggesting that we adjust mitigation strategies
if Al enables new biological attacks, and proposes monitoring if labs achieve recursive self-
improvement and loss-of-control risks grow exponentially.
But nowhere does he explain how his framework would handle a harm we can't iterate our
way out of: an engineered pandemic, say, or a catastrophic cyberattack. He casts falling
behind China as the risk that dwarfs all others, and suggests that any precaution that slows
down US releases by even a month itself is a safety hazard. It's a world where shipping
open-weights models fast and to everyone is the only safe strategy - which, conveniently,
means that the safest possible world is one where Meta can execute its roadmap
unimpeded.

posts.text: Talked to Replit CEO Amjad Masad about how he dealt with the feeling that "everything I worked for is kind of moot" following the rapid improvement of coding tools https://www.platformer.news/replit-amjad-massad-interview-coding-design-jobs/
posts.html: Talked to Replit CEO Amjad Masad about how he dealt with the feeling that "everything I worked for is kind of moot" following the rapid improvement of coding tools https://www.platformer.news/replit-amjad-massad-interview-coding-design-jobs/

media.alt:
Now, in 2025, when we started getting Opus and the new Claude models, I was like, okay, I
need to be honest with myself. My entire life mission around teaching people coding is
changing. You don't need to code anymore. And I started building things without looking at
the code — this was before Karpathy even coined "vibe coding." So I was on TBPN, and I
said it. It was actually kind of a painful moment, because here you are, you dedicated your
life — I've been working on making coding easier for literally 15 years, most of my adult life
— and I'm saying everything that I worked toward is kind of moot, and the way forward is
that we make programming so easy that anyone could do it.

posts.text: Why are Snap, LinkedIn, and Substack turning away from slop while Meta and TikTok embrace it? It comes down to what the platforms promise their user bases https://www.platformer.news/slop-restrictions-linkedin-substack-snap/
posts.html: Why are Snap, LinkedIn, and Substack turning away from slop while Meta and TikTok embrace it? It comes down to what the platforms promise their user bases https://www.platformer.news/slop-restrictions-linkedin-substack-snap/

media.alt:
This summer, we appear to be moving into slop's third era. The first was characterized by
near-universal disdain for laughable writing and six-fingered humans; the second by the
surprising popularity of slop shows like "Fruit Love Island." In the third era of slop, platforms
are rethinking their approaches to Al-generated content based on what their user bases
need from them — and vice-versa. Platforms that place a premium on trust are realizing
just how quickly slop can erode it. And platforms that don't are ready to give us as much
slop as we can handle.

posts.author: Casey Newton
posts.text: I talked to the CEO of one of the only good AI *product* companies — Chris Pedregal of Granola — about what an AI notetaker learns about a company, and what bosses keep asking him to do with it https://www.platformer.news/granola-chris-pedregal-interview/
posts.html: I talked to the CEO of one of the only good AI *product* companies — Chris Pedregal of Granola — about what an AI notetaker learns about a company, and what bosses keep asking him to do with it https://www.platformer.news/granola-chris-pedregal-interview/

media.alt:
Pedregal: I think it's an opportunity if it's bottoms-up, and I think it stresses me out if it's
top-down. If you're saying, I don't think my manager is very good — help me navigate how I
should work with my manager — I think that's great. I think it's empowering. CEOs will ask
us all the time, saying: I want everyone at my company using Granola, and I want access to
all the transcripts and all the notes to run the queries that you're talking about. And we say
no. That's not what the tool is built for. You can set that up if you want, but then you have
to create a company culture and set an expectation, and everyone needs to share their
notes and understand what they're getting into. But there's no backdoor way. I think that's
a slippery slope. If you have a backdoor way for someone in power to use all this context to
make judgment calls in that way, that doesn't feel right to me, and that's not a future we
want to build towards.

posts.text: Wrote about AI denialism on Bluesky https://www.platformer.news/a-big-week-for-ai-denialism/
posts.html: Wrote about AI denialism on Bluesky https://www.platformer.news/a-big-week-for-ai-denialism/

media.alt:
What all of these arguments have in common is that they serve as invitations to stop
thinking about Al.
Who cares? It's just marketing.
Who cares? They're just doing what they were programmed to.
Who cares? It's not like they're sentient.
I understand the appeal of arguments like these. The implications of an exponential takeoff
in Al capabilities are extremely worrisome. They range from advanced cyberattacks like the
one Hugging Face just endured to job loss, novel bioweapons, expanded systems for
surveillance and repression, and autonomous weaponry. Who wants to think about any of
that, if they don't have to?
